To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
carotenoid and sterol metabolites of alga-derived carotenoids and sterols were identified in Dreissena bugensisis, and LC-PDA/APCI itMS is a useful technique for this type of analysis.

LC-PDA and LC-APCIitMS analyses of hydrolyzed extracts revealed carotenoid precursers and C27-sterol triols in Dreissena bugenesis, and the LC retention times correlated to solubilty parameters for 12 standards and 3 polar carotenoid and sterol metabolites.

the carotenoid and sterol metabolites from the dreissenid mussel Dreissene bugensis, identified using liquid chromatography (HPLC) and mass spectrometry, include fucoxanthin and violaxanthin, as well as two unknowns tentatively identified as C27-steryl esters, which are the first such identification of these metabolites in a freshwater bivalve.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of LC-MS for the identification of carotenoid and steryl metabolites from algal precursors, in hydrolyzed and unhydrolyzed dreissenid extracts.
the identification of carotenoid and sterol metabolites in hydrolyzed Dreissena bugensi extracts, and the application of LC-MS for this purpose.
identifying carotenoid and sterol precursors of carotenoid and steryl ester metabolites, in Dreissenid tissues and fecal pellets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

LC-PDA-MS analyses of carotenoid and steryl triol products of hydrolysis of Dreissena carotenyl-esters revealed the carotenoid and sterol precursors, but the LC-PDA-APCIitMS analyses did not reveal the linkage of the carotenoid metabolite to the oxysterol.

LC-PDA/APCI-MS analysis of carotenyl- and oxysteryl-FAEs from D. bugensis, after hydrolysis, revealed that the major carotenoid precursory compounds are FOH and MX and that C27-steryl-FAEs are major precursors to the oxysterols.

the LC-PDA/APCI-MS analysis of the hydrolyzed carotenoid esters of D. bugensis revealed that the dominant carotenoids were derived from the diet, and that the dominant oxysterols were likely derived from the host.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LC with a PDA detector and LC-MS with an APCIitMS or other soft ionization source would provide a powerful tool for carotenoid and carotenyl- ester analysis in biological samples.
LC-PDA-APCiitMS is a useful tool for the analysis of complex carotenoid and sterol mixtures in the presence of bile salts.
LC-PDA/APCI-MS analysis of carotenoid and sterol metabolites in Dreissena is feasible, but requires careful optimization of sample preparation and LC-MS conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LC-PDA and LC-APCIitMS can be used together to identify the carotene and oxysterol metabolites of alga-derived carotenoid esters in dreissenid extracts.
LC-PDA-APCIitMS is a powerful combination of analytical techniques to identify carotenoid precursers to carotenyl-esters in hydrolyzed samples.
LC-MS analysis, using PDA and APCIitMS detectors, is a valuable approach to identify carotenoid and steryl triol products from carotenoid esters, which may be useful for other applications.
